title: ⚡ Bolt: Optimize bulk discount code generation with DB batching
body:
## 💡 What
Replaced sequential `.run()` calls with `env.DB.batch()` during bulk discount code generation in `worker/routes/discountsRoutes.js`, including a sequential fallback for constraint collisions.

## 🎯 Why
Generating and inserting multiple unique discount codes via `/generate-codes` caused a severe N+1 latency bottleneck by executing separate database queries for every code within a for-loop.

## 📊 Impact
Reduces D1 database roundtrips from `N` to `ceil(N/100)`, drastically decreasing API latency when merchants generate large quantities of promotional codes.

## 🔬 Measurement
Identified via code inspection (`grep -r ".run()" worker/routes/` and reviewing bulk loops). Expected impact is a linear reduction in database execution latency proportional to the number of generated codes.

## 🛡️ Safety
The optimization strictly preserves behavior. It groups `INSERT` statements into a batch. Crucially, if a batch fails (e.g. D1 unique constraint rollback), a `catch` block correctly falls back to sequential inserts to isolate collisions and save valid codes. Mock databases in tests are handled via the `typeof env.DB.batch === 'function'` check.

## ✅ Verification
Executed `node --test tests/discounts-engine.test.mjs` and `node tests/security-regression.test.mjs` locally. All tests pass successfully.

## 📁 Scope
- `worker/routes/discountsRoutes.js`
